# Sirach Chapter 43 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 43 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Sirach 43 is the grandest passage in the entire book — a sustained cosmic hymn praising God through the phenomena of creation: sun (vv. 2–5), moon (vv. 6–8), stars (vv. 9–10), rainbow (vv. 11–12), snow and hail and storm (vv. 13–20), dew and mist (vv. 21–22), sea (vv. 23–25), culminating in the great declaration of v. 27. The language must be elevated throughout.

**Key decisions:**
- v. 27: "He is the all" (autos estin to pan) — SOPHIA retains the Greek with minimal gloss. This is nearly pantheistic; Ben Sira comes as close as any Jewish text of his era to the Stoic doctrine that God is identical with the sum of all things. The translation must not soften this. ALL THREE agents render it identically: "He is the all." SOPHIA retains this without change.
- v. 1: "clear firmament" vs. "vault of heaven" — "firmament" echoes Genesis 1 (raqia/stereōma); SOPHIA retains "clear firmament" for the scriptural resonance.
- v. 8: "military instrument" (EMET) vs. "instrument of the host" (LOGOS) — the moon as a signal for military/calendrical purposes. SOPHIA: "instrument of the host on high" for the military-celestial double meaning.
- v. 26: "all things hold together" (synechō) — resonates with Col. 1:17. Retain.
- v. 30: The threefold exhortation structure must be preserved as three clauses.

---

**43:1** The crown of the heights above is the clear firmament; the appearance of the sky is a vision of glory.

**43:2** The sun, when it appears, proclaims as it rises — what a marvelous creation, the work of the Most High!

**43:3** At noon it parches the land; and who can endure its scorching heat?

**43:4** A man stoking a furnace works in burning heat, but the sun scorches the mountains three times more; breathing out fiery vapors and shooting out blinding rays, it dazzles the eyes.

**43:5** Great is the Lord who made it! At his word it runs swiftly on its course.

**43:6** The moon also marks the times in all its phases — a sign of seasons and an everlasting marker.

**43:7** From the moon comes the reckoning of feast days; it is a light that wanes when it has reached its full.

**43:8** The month is named after the moon, increasing marvelously as it changes; it is an instrument of the host on high, shining brilliantly in the firmament of heaven.

**43:9** The splendor of the stars is the glory of the skies; a glittering ornament in the heights of the Lord.

**43:10** At the word of the Holy One they stand in due order, and they never slacken at their watch.

**43:11** Look at the rainbow and bless its Maker; it blazes with extraordinary beauty.

**43:12** It arcs across the sky with its radiant bow, drawn by the hands of the Most High.

**43:13** By his command he sends driving snow, and hurls down flashes of his judgment.

**43:14** Therefore the storehouses are opened, and the clouds fly out like birds.

**43:15** In his majesty he makes the clouds dense, and the hailstones are broken in pieces.

**43:16** The voice of his thunder makes the earth writhe; the storm from the north and the whirlwind.

**43:17** Like birds alighting, he scatters the snowflakes; they settle like locusts descending.

**43:18** The eye marvels at the beauty of their whiteness, and the heart is struck with wonder at their falling.

**43:19** He pours out frost upon the earth like salt; when it freezes it becomes bristling points of ice.

**43:20** The cold north wind blows and ice forms over the water; it settles on every pool, and the water puts on a coat of armor.

**43:21** It consumes the mountains and scorches the wilderness; it burns fresh green grass like fire.

**43:22** A sudden mist brings healing to all these; dew falling after heat brings relief.

**43:23** By his counsel he has stilled the ocean deep and planted islands in it.

**43:24** Those who sail the sea tell of its dangers; we hear them and are struck with astonishment.

**43:25** For in it are his most astonishing works: all manner of strange and varied creatures, the whole teeming world of living things and the great sea monsters.

**43:26** Because of him his messenger succeeds; and by his word all things hold together.

**43:27** We could say more, and still we could never say enough; let the final word be: He is the all.

**43:28** Where shall we find the strength to praise him? For he is greater than all his works.

**43:29** The Lord is awesome and exceedingly great, and his power is wonderful.

**43:30** Exalt the Lord as highly as you can, for he will surpass even that. When you exalt him, redouble your strength; do not grow weary, for you cannot reach the end.

**43:31** Who has seen him and can describe him? And who can praise him as he truly is?

**43:32** Many things greater than these remain hidden; we have seen but few of his works.

**43:33** For the Lord made all things, and to the devout he has given wisdom.
